title: Streamlined model admission: clarity checklist for pinning & compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Clarify requirements and produce an operational checklist for admitting new open-models into the Redwood Model Catalog. Focus areas: when to require version pinning, how to populate compatibility_notes, automated vs manual signals for runtime compatibility, and minimal acceptance criteria for initial rollout.
background: We currently have divergent practices across teams for ingesting community models (unverified weights) into the catalog. This results in: inconsistent pinning (some entries unpinned and later break runtime), sparse compatibility_notes, and surprise regressions in hosted and dedicated deployments. PMs, runtime engineering, and model-ops need a single source of truth that defines gating, metadata, and acceptance criteria for onboarding open models.
goals: Define clear rules for when a model variant must be pinned vs allowed to float
Specify minimal compatibility_notes schema and required fields for each catalog entry
Create an operational checklist (manual + automated) that runtime/QA uses to accept an intake
Reduce post-admission runtime incidents tied to unpinned or undocumented variants by 80% in the next quarter
out_of_scope: Rewriting the entire model ingestion UI (this is purely requirements and checklist work)
Implementing pinning enforcement in the runtime (engineers will pick up separate tickets)
Policy for proprietary/partner models (handled in the partner onboarding flow)
in_scope: Checklist items for automated tests and manual reviews
proposed_requirements: Requirement 1: If an open-model variant contains community weights (non-Redwood verified) and has fewer than 3 successful perf profiles in QA, it must be pinned to a specific artifact hash or release tag.

Requirement 2: Every catalog entry must include a compatibility_notes field containing: runtime-tested-sequences, known-unsupported-features (e.g., kv-cache size, rotary embeddings), recommended-quantization, and fallbacks-for-low-memory. Each must have at least one example or numeric threshold where applicable.

Requirement 3: Add automated sanity checks on ingest: model architecture parsing, tokenizer mapping validation, kv-cache plausibility check, and a smoke generation test (10 prompt seeds) with token-level failure/error logging.
Requirement 4: If automated checks flag a mismatch (e.g., tokenizer vs model vocab), entry is flagged 'manual-review' and cannot be published until triaged by runtime engineering.

Requirement 5: Provide metadata fields that declare compatibility tier: compatible-hosted, compatible-dedicated, compatible-private (each a boolean string). If hosted=false, the catalog must display a human-readable explanation.

Requirement 6: Define a default pin-fallback policy: when a runtime regression is detected on an unpinned variant, automatically fallback to the most recent pinned variant of the same model family (if available) and create a rollback changelog entry.
Requirement 7: Capture owner and contact fields on the entry (team, triage-owner-email) and require an SLA for triage (48 business hours) on flagged ingests.
acceptance_criteria: A single-page checklist doc is published to Confluence and linked from the intake UI
The checklist includes step-by-step gating for: auto-pass, auto-fail, manual-review, and temporary pin suggestion
All fields in compatibility_notes are documented with examples and at least two sample model entries updated to the new schema
A short automated test harness is defined (commands + expected outputs) that runtime engineering can implement to run ingest sanity checks
Product and runtime engineering sign-off recorded as comments on this ticket
Hand-off ticket(s) created for engineering work to enforce pinning rules in catalog ingestion pipeline
rollout_plan: Week 0: Draft checklist and circulate to runtime, model-ops, and docs for feedback
Week 1: Iterate on checklist with concrete examples and produce compatibility_notes template
Week 2: Publish Confluence doc and update two pilot catalog entries to the new schema
Week 3: Run intake on 5 recent community models as a dry-run and collect issues
Week 4: Finalize acceptance criteria and create engineering tickets for enforcement; mark this checklist as 'Adopted'
risks_mitigations: Risk: Overly strict pinning could block high-quality community models. Mitigation: include an expedited review path with a dedicated reviewer and SLAs.
Risk: Teams may treat compatibility_notes as boilerplate. Mitigation: require one example-driven item per compatibility field and include reviewer checklist items to validate examples.
Risk: Automation false-positives create noise. Mitigation: log confidence scores and provide a triage dashboard to adjust thresholds quickly.
discussion_notes: 03/03: Runtime expressed concern about automatic fallback complexity; recommended starting with a 'suggested fallback' notification rather than enforced behavior
03/05: Model-ops suggested adding a 'confidence' numeric field (0-100) to the catalog entry for automated decisions; added to proposed requirements as optional follow-up
03/10: Docs reviewed compatibility_notes template and asked for 2 real-world examples to include in the public docs
notes_for_engineering: Provide a lightweight CLI command that runs the ingestion sanity checks locally and returns a machine-readable report
Expose a small API endpoint for the catalog UI to query compatibility tier booleans
Implement changelog entries on fallback events and ensure they reference the pinned artifact hash
